land.text: Kerman province (Kirman): the one territory the pages name

predecessors.note: Kerman was Khwarazmian after 'Kerman was annexed by the Khwarezmid Empire in 1196' (Kerman Seljuk page); the Baraq Hajib page has him defeat the local governor Shuja ad-Din Abul-Qasim and take Kirman with help from Jalal ad-Din. The Qutlugh-Khanids infobox lists the Khwarazmian Empire as 'succeeded by' (a vassal relation, not a predecessor).

land.text: Kerman province (Kirman): the one territory the pages name

predecessors.note: The infobox lists Qara Khitai as 'preceded by'; the founder 'emigrated from the Qara Khitai (Western Liao dynasty) during the collapse of the realm' (Qutlugh-Khanids page). The Qara Khitai never held Kerman; the link is the dynasty's origin.

land.text: Kerman province (Kirman): the one territory the pages name

successors.note: 'The dynasty was removed from power by the Ilkhanid ruler Öljaitü' in 1306 (Qutlugh-Khanids page). The infobox lists 'Khwarazmian Empire', 'Mongol Empire' and 'Ilkhanate' as succeeded by; the Ilkhanate is the one that took the land.

capitals.name: Kerman
capitals.note: The page lists no capital; it says the dynasty 'ruled over Kirman' and the Baraq Hajib page has the siege and conquest of Kirman. Bridge at confidence 1.

rulers.note: The last of the Qutlugh Khans; he 'escaped to Shiraz' when Öljaitü ended the dynasty.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria lacks the Qutlugh-Khanids). The page says the dynasty 'ruled over Kirman (in present-day Kerman province, Iran) from 1222 to 1306' and names no other territory: Makran, Hormuz, Oman and Fars do not appear (Shiraz is named only as the refuge of the last Qutlugh Khan in 1306). Drawn as Kerman province for the whole span. Fixed-frontier claims are not made.

ledger.note: 1222: Baraq Hajib founds the dynasty in Kerman. Infobox 'Established: 1222'; the dynasty 'ruled over Kirman (in present-day Kerman province, Iran) from 1222 to 1306'. The Baraq Hajib page, undated: he came to Kerman as a commander in Purshah's army, defeated the local governor Shuja ad-Din Abul-Qasim 'thanks to defection of Turks' and, helped by Jalal ad-Din, took Kirman. The khwarezmid-empire dossier has Kerman confirmed under him in 1224.

notes:
A state Cliopatria lacks (cliopatria_names []). Two pages opened (plus the Kerman Seljuk page used in the earlier dossier for the 1196 annexation). Slug 'qutlugh-khanids' follows the validator's slugify(name) rule (the khwarezmid-empire dossier's notes write 'Qutlughkhanids' in prose, not as a slug); the Wikipedia title is Qutlugh-Khanids. Wikidata id not obtainable: null.
Territory: the Qutlugh-Khanids page says only that the dynasty 'ruled over Kirman (in present-day Kerman province, Iran) from 1222 to 1306'. No Makran, Hormuz, Oman or Fars appears, so the single keyframe is Kerman province.
Status: the page says the dynasty was 'originally an independent entity' and 'subsequently ruled as vassals of the Khwarazmian Empire, the Mongol Empire and the Ilkhanate'; Baraq Hajib 'later submitted to the Mongol Empire' (sent his son to Ögedei's court shortly before his death in 1234/5) and Kutlugh Turkan 'had been granted autonomy by Abaqa Khan'. Vassal events are recorded in the suzerain dossiers: the khwarezmid-empire dossier has a 1224 vassal_start for Kerman under 'Burak Hajib of Kerman (Qara Khitai of Kerman)' with no matching vassal_end; ulus-of-hulegu carries no Kerman vassal_start (undated on the pages) and no 1306 gain (this dossier's 1306 loss and dissolve name ulus-of-hulegu as counterpart).
Rulers: the page's list overlaps in the 1250s-1280s (Hajjaj 1257-1267/8 with Kutlugh Turkan 1257-1282); the strip here starts Kutlugh Turkan in 1267 and the page's years are in the notes. Baraq Hajib's end year is 1235 on the list and 1234/5 on his page.
Not settled: when Baraq took Kerman (the Baraq Hajib page is undated: he first came with Purshah's army, defeated the governor, and Jalal ad-Din helped; it also records Purshah's flight to Kirman in 1228 and Baraq forcing him to give his mother's hand in marriage), the Qara Khitai link (an origin, not a predecessor holding Kerman), and the Muzaffarids' rise (the Qutlugh-Khanids page names only an escape to Shiraz).
Gazetteer names used that it lacks: none new.
